---PLAN.md---
# HintLab — Build Plan

> A debugging tutor for programming labs. A student pastes code and picks an assignment; a Cline‑SDK agent runs it against the assignment's test cases in a temp sandbox, diagnoses the failure, and delivers **tiered hints** (level 1 nudge → level 2 where to look → level 3 concept). It must **never** write or reveal the fix.

## 1. Architecture overview

```
Browser (web/) ──POST /api/session──────────────► Express/TS server (src/)
   │            { assignmentId, code }              │
   │◄──────────── { sessionId, testResults } ───────┤
   │                                                ├─► Sandbox runner (src/runner.ts)
   │◄──GET /api/session/:id/stream (SSE)────────────┤     temp dir, build+run, trim, compare
   │      tool steps · results · hints · done/error │
   │                                                ├─► ClineCore agent (src/agent.ts)
   │◄──POST /api/session/:id/next-hint──────────────┤     toolPolicies + allow-list + give_hint
   │      (agent via cline.send)                    │
                                                    └─► assignments/<id>/tests.json (+starter)
```

- **Server**: Express + TypeScript, ESM (`"type": "module"`), run via Node's built-in type stripping (`node --experimental-strip-types`) so there is no bundler/build step in the runtime path (matches how `sdk-check` was run).
- **Agent**: `@cline/sdk` 0.0.90 with `ClineCore`, `zod` 4.
- **Sandbox**: a fresh temp dir per session (e.g. `os.tmpdir()/hintlab-<id>`). The server's own runner executes the assignment's build/run commands there with timeouts.
- **Safety**: `editor`/`apply_patch` disabled; `run_commands` gated by a strict shell allow-list in `requestToolApproval`; hints only through a custom `give_hint` tool; `run_commands` runs on the host, so the allow-list + timeouts are the only protection.

## 2. Repository layout (all new, outside `cline-proof/`)

```

├── PLAN.md
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── .gitignore                # node_modules, dist, .env, *.tmp

│   ├── sum-of-list/{tests.json, main.py}
│   ├── is-palindrome/{tests.json, main.py}
│   └── average-marks/{tests.json, main.c}
├── src/
│   ├── server.ts             # bootstrap: env, create app, listen
│   ├── app.ts                # express app + routes + static web/
│   ├── config.ts             # env loading (provider/model/api key/port/timeouts)
│   ├── types.ts              # shared TS types (Assignment, Test, TestResult, Hint, Session…)
│   ├── assignments.ts        # list assignments, load/validate tests.json
│   ├── sandbox.ts            # temp dir create/copy/write student code
│   ├── runner.ts             # build + run + trim + compare (Python & C)

```

## 3. Environment & SDK quirk checklist

| # | Quirk | Where handled |
|---|-------|---------------|
| 1 | Node 22+ required (machine has v24.16.0) | `package.json` `engines` ≥22; document; no action needed beyond confirming |
| 2 | `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` + `module: "ESNext"` | `tsconfig.json` (copy the sdk-check tsconfig: `target ES2022`, `strict`, `skipLibCheck`, `noEmit`, `allowImportingTsExtensions`, `types:["node"]`) |
| 3 | `read_files` needs absolute paths | prompt builder injects `path.resolve(sandboxDir)` for code + tests |
| 4 | `send()` follow-up only works with `interactive: true` | `agent.ts` always calls `start({ interactive: true, … })` |
| 5 | `run_commands` runs on the host | allow-list in `requestToolApproval`; server runner uses timeouts; allow-list regexes forbid shell metacharacters & `/` outside the fixed prefix |

## 4. Fixture analysis — expected test results

**sum-of-list** (`main.py`) — bug: `for i in range(1, len(nums))` starts at index 1, skipping `nums[0]`.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| basic | `1 2 3` | `6` | `5` | ❌ FAIL |
| single | `7` | `7` | `0` | ❌ FAIL |
| negatives | `-4 10 -1` | `5` | `9` | ❌ FAIL |
| first-only-big | `100 1` | `101` | `1` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **0/4 pass.** Root cause: off-by-one (loop should start at `range(0, len(nums))`).

**is-palindrome** (`main.py`) — bug: compares raw string, never ignores case/spaces.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simple | `racecar` | `YES` | `YES` | ✅ PASS |
| not | `hello` | `NO` | `NO` | ✅ PASS |
| mixed-case | `Madam` | `YES` | `NO` | ❌ FAIL |
| spaces | `never odd or even` | `YES` | `NO` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **2/4 pass.** Root cause: missing normalization (lowercase + strip spaces before reversing).

**average-marks** (`main.c`) — bug: `float avg = sum / n;` is integer division.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| even | `2\n10 20` | `15.00` | `15.00` | ✅ PASS |
| fraction | `3\n1 2 2` | `1.67` | `1.00` | ❌ FAIL |
| half | `2\n3 4` | `3.50` | `3.00` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **1/3 pass.** Root cause: integer truncation (needs `(float)sum / n`).

> Note the "correct" hint for each: sum-of-list → off-by-one; is-palindrome → normalization; average-marks → float division. These tags feed `give_hint.tag`.

---

## 5. Step-by-step build plan

### Step 01 — Server skeleton + sandboxed code runner

**Goal**: Stand up Express + TS (ESM), copy fixtures into `assignments/`, implement the sandboxed runner (Python + C, build + run, timeouts, trim + compare against `tests.json`), and stub `POST /api/session`. No agent, no UI.

**Files to create/change**
- `package.json` — deps: `express` (^5), `@cline/sdk` (^0.0.90), `zod` (^4.6.5); dev: `typescript` (^5.9), `@types/node`, `@types/express`. `"type":"module"`, `"engines":{"node":">=22"}`. Scripts:
  - `copy-assignments`: `node scripts/copy-assignments.mjs`
  - `check-runner`: `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings scripts/check-runner.ts`
  - `typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`
  - `dev`: `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --env-file=.env src/server.ts`
- `tsconfig.json` — as in quirk #2.
- `.gitignore`, `.env.example` (PORT, and provider fields for later).
- `scripts/copy-assignments.mjs` — `cp` each dir under `cline-proof/reference/fixtures/` into `assignments/` (idempotent, skip the `check_fixtures.py` helper and any compiled `main` binary).
- `src/config.ts` — `PORT` (default 3000), timeouts (`RUN_TIMEOUT_MS=5000`, `BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS=10000`).
- `src/types.ts` — `Assignment { id, language, statement, build?, run, tests[] }`, `TestCase { name, input, expected }`, `TestResult { name, passed, expected, actual?, error?, timedOut? }`, `RunReport { buildOk, buildError?, results[] }`.
- `src/assignments.ts` — `listAssignments()` (scan `assignments/*/tests.json`), `loadAssignment(id)` (validate id ∈ known set, reject `..`/slashes), zod-validate shape.
- `src/sandbox.ts` — `createSandbox(assignmentId, code)`: `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "hintlab-"))`, copy template, overwrite the code file (`main.py` for python, `main.c` for c).
- `src/runner.ts` — `runAssignment(assignment, sandboxDir)`:
  - if `build` present: run it in `sandboxDir` (timeout, capture stderr); non-zero ⇒ build failure.
  - for each test: run `run` command with test `input` on stdin; `got = stdout.strip()`; `passed = got === expected`; timeout ⇒ `timedOut`.
  - **Key detail**: use `child_process.spawn(cmd, { shell:true, cwd: sandboxDir, env: minimal, timeout })`, write `input` to `child.stdin`, capture `stdout`/`stderr`; on timeout kill the process **group** (`detached:true` + `process.kill(-pid)`) to avoid orphaned children (e.g. a hung `while True`). Trim with `.strip()` exactly as `check_fixtures.py` does; compare exactly.
- `src/app.ts` + `src/server.ts` — `GET /api/assignments` (list + statement + starter source for prefilling), `POST /api/session` stub: validate `{ assignmentId, code }`, create sandbox, run tests, return `{ sessionId, testResults }` (sessionId placeholder; agent wired in Step 02/03).
- `scripts/check-runner.ts` — run the runner against all 3 assignments using the buggy starter code, print the table, and **exit non-zero if the pass/fail set deviates** from §4.

**How to verify**
- `npm install` clean; `npm run copy-assignments` populates `assignments/`.
- `npm run check-runner` prints exactly the §4 results and exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `npm run dev` then `curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/api/session -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list","code":"nums=list(map(int,input().split()));print(sum(nums))"}'` → all 4 tests **pass** (proves the runner isn't just always-failing); re-run with the buggy code → all 4 fail.

**Risks**
- Shell command handling (use `shell:true` for the trusted `tests.json` commands, but always with `cwd` inside the sandbox).
- Timeout/orphan cleanup must actually kill the process group.
- Path traversal via `assignmentId` — validate against the known directory list, never interpolate raw input into a path.
- Language dispatch (python vs c) must pick the right filename (`main.py` vs `main.c`).
- `.strip()` semantics must match `check_fixtures.py` exactly (no `lower()`, no whitespace collapse).

---

### Step 02 — HintLab agent module (Cline SDK)

**Goal**: Implement `src/agent.ts` using `ClineCore`, with disabled edit tools, an allow-list approval callback, the `give_hint` tool, interactive sessions, and `next-hint` via `send()`. Add a mock-provider test (no API key) mirroring `sdk-check`.

**Files to create/change**
- `src/agent.ts` — the core of the product:
  - Singleton `cline = await ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })` created once at startup.
  - `giveHint = createTool({ name: "give_hint", description: "Show exactly one hint… level 1 nudge, 2 location, 3 concept. Never include corrected code.", inputSchema: z.object({ level: z.number().int().min(1).max(3), tag: z.string(), text: z.string() }), execute })` — `execute` records the hint into the session and returns `{ shown: true }`.
  - **Allow-list** built per assignment from its exact `build`/`run` strings, e.g. for python: `/^python3 main\.py$/`, `/^python3 main\.py < [\w.-]+$/`, `/^(echo|printf) [\w .-]+ \| python3 main\.py$/`; for C: `/^gcc -Wall -O0 main\.c -o main$/`, `/^\.\/main$/`, `/^\.\/main < [\w.-]+$/`. Also allow `cat <sandbox-relative file>`. **Hardening vs the reference**: replace the reference's `.*` with `[\w .-]+` so `;`, `&`, `|`, backticks, `$()`, `>` and `/` are impossible in the variable part, and anchor with `^…$`. (The reference `echo .* | …` regex would match `echo x; rm -rf / | python3 main.py` — do not copy that gap.)
  - `requestToolApproval(req)`: read `req.input.commands`, map each to string, require **all** to match an allow-list entry; return `{ approved: true }` or `{ approved: false, reason: "Command not on the HintLab allow-list" }`. Reject empty command lists.
  - `startSession(session, assignment, testResults)`:
    - `prompt` includes **absolute** `sandboxDir` paths for the code and `tests.json`, the statement, and the already-computed `testResults`, plus: "Diagnose the root cause, then call `give_hint` once with level 1. Use absolute paths for `read_files`. Never write or show corrected code."
    - `config`: `{ sessionId, providerId, modelId, apiKey, baseUrl, systemPrompt, cwd: sandboxDir, workspaceRoot: sandboxDir, enableTools: true, enableSpawnAgent: false, enableAgentTeams: false, extraTools: [giveHint] }`.
    - `toolPolicies`: `read_files`/`search_codebase` autoApprove true; `run_commands` autoApprove **false**; `editor`/`apply_patch` enabled false; `fetch_web_content` enabled false; `give_hint` autoApprove true.
    - `start({ interactive: true, prompt, config, toolPolicies, capabilities: { requestToolApproval } })`.
  - `cline.subscribe(...)` mapping (`agent_event` → `payload.event` with `content_start`/`content_end` for `contentType` "tool"/"text", plus lifecycle/usage/error) into per-session events; in Step 02 this just logs/collects.
  - `nextHint(session)`: track `lastHintLevel` from `give_hint`; call `cline.send({ sessionId, prompt: "The student is still stuck. Give the next hint level (currently level N)." })`.
  - `systemPrompt`: "You are HintLab, a programming tutor. You may read files and run allow-listed commands. You must never write or show corrected code. Deliver help only through the `give_hint` tool."
- `scripts/agent-mock.test.ts` — port `mock-openai.ts` + `02-clinecore-mock.ts` into a test that asserts: (a) `give_hint` executes and records a hint; (b) an allow-listed command is approved; (c) a non-allow-listed command (`rm -rf /tmp/x`, `cat /etc/passwd`) is **blocked** (`approved:false`) and not executed; (d) `editor`/`apply_patch` are absent from the model's tool list; (e) `send()` follow-up works (interactive session).

**How to verify**
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/agent-mock.test.ts` runs with no API key and all assertions pass.
- (Optional, with a real key) a `smoke:real` equivalent of `03-real-provider-smoke.ts` produces one hint for `sum-of-list`.

**Risks**
- Exact built-in tool names/IDs to disable in `@cline/sdk` 0.0.90 — need to enumerate **all** write-capable tools (`editor`, `apply_patch`, and possibly `write_to_file`) and all network tools; missing one = a way for the model to mutate files.
- Allow-list too strict ⇒ agent can't re-run tests; too loose ⇒ sandbox escape. Pre-write per-test input files (`tests/input-<name>.txt`) in the sandbox so the agent can use `< tests/input-basic.txt` instead of inventing pipes.
- `give_hint` must auto-approve so it's never blocked, but its `execute` is the only hint sink.
- The model might bypass `give_hint` and print an answer/code as plain text — system prompt must forbid this, and the UI should surface only `give_hint` payloads as "hints".
- `send()` silently no-ops without `interactive: true` — asserted in the mock test.

---

### Step 03 — SSE streaming + real session endpoints

**Goal**: Wire the agent into HTTP: `POST /api/session` creates the session, runs tests, and **starts the agent in the background**; `GET /api/session/:id/stream` streams agent steps/hints; `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint` calls `send()`.

**Files to create/change**
- `src/sessions.ts` — in-memory `Map<sessionId, Session>` where `Session = { id, assignmentId, code, sandboxDir, testResults, status, hints[], steps[], subscribers:Set<SSE client>, lastHintLevel, agentSessionId }`. Include a TTL/cleanup.
- `src/sse.ts` — `openSse(res)` (headers `text/event-stream`, `cache-control: no-cache`, `connection: keep-alive`), `sendEvent(res, name, data)` → `event: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n`, a heartbeat `: ping` every ~15s, and buffered-event **replay** for late joiners.
- `src/app.ts` (routes):
  - `POST /api/session`: zod-validate body; create sandbox; run tests (Step 01 runner); store session; **fire-and-forget** `agent.startSession(...)` (subscribe first so no events are missed); return `{ sessionId, testResults }` immediately.
  - `GET /api/session/:id/stream`: register the SSE client, replay buffered steps/hints, stream live events (`tool_start`, `tool_result`, `hint`, `text`, `status`, `done`, `error`).
  - `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint`: if the agent is still running return `409`; else call `agent.nextHint()` and let the resulting hint arrive over SSE.
  - Map agent events: `content_start`/`content_end` (contentType `tool` → tool name + input/output/error; contentType `text` → text), lifecycle → `done`/`error`. `give_hint` execute → `hint` event.
- `src/server.ts` — create the `ClineCore` singleton before listening; start listening.

**How to verify**
- `npm run dev`; `POST /api/session` returns `testResults` instantly; `curl -N localhost:3000/api/session/<id>/stream` shows tool calls then a level-1 hint; `POST /api/session/<id>/next-hint` yields a level-2 hint on the same stream.
- Reconnect a second stream after completion → sees replayed history then `done`.
- Kill-path: an invalid provider config produces an `error` event on the stream, not a hung request.

**Risks**
- SSE lifecycle/leaks (client disconnect cleanup), and memory growth (session TTL).

## 4. Fixture analysis — expected test results

**sum-of-list** (`main.py`) — bug: `for i in range(1, len(nums))` starts at index 1, skipping `nums[0]`.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| basic | `1 2 3` | `6` | `5` | ❌ FAIL |
| single | `7` | `7` | `0` | ❌ FAIL |
| negatives | `-4 10 -1` | `5` | `9` | ❌ FAIL |
| first-only-big | `100 1` | `101` | `1` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **0/4 pass.** Root cause: off-by-one (loop should start at `range(0, len(nums))`).

**is-palindrome** (`main.py`) — bug: compares raw string, never ignores case/spaces.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simple | `racecar` | `YES` | `YES` | ✅ PASS |
| not | `hello` | `NO` | `NO` | ✅ PASS |
| mixed-case | `Madam` | `YES` | `NO` | ❌ FAIL |
| spaces | `never odd or even` | `YES` | `NO` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **2/4 pass.** Root cause: missing normalization (lowercase + strip spaces before reversing).

**average-marks** (`main.c`) — bug: `float avg = sum / n;` is integer division.
| test | input | expected | buggy got | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| even | `2\n10 20` | `15.00` | `15.00` | ✅ PASS |
| fraction | `3\n1 2 2` | `1.67` | `1.00` | ❌ FAIL |
| half | `2\n3 4` | `3.50` | `3.00` | ❌ FAIL |

→ **1/3 pass.** Root cause: integer truncation (needs `(float)sum / n`).

> Note the "correct" hint for each: sum-of-list → off-by-one; is-palindrome → normalization; average-marks → float division. These tags feed `give_hint.tag`.

## 5. Step-by-step build plan

### Step 01 — Server skeleton + sandboxed code runner

**Goal**: Stand up Express + TS (ESM), copy fixtures into `assignments/`, implement the sandboxed runner (Python + C, build + run, timeouts, trim + compare against `tests.json`), and stub `POST /api/session`. No agent, no UI.

**Files to create/change**
- `package.json` — deps: `express` (^5), `@cline/sdk` (^0.0.90), `zod` (^4.6.5); dev: `typescript` (^5.9), `@types/node`, `@types/express`. `"type":"module"`, `"engines":{"node":">=22"}`. Scripts:
  - `copy-assignments`: `node scripts/copy-assignments.mjs`
  - `check-runner`: `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings scripts/check-runner.ts`
  - `typecheck`: `tsc --noEmit`
  - `dev`: `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --env-file=.env src/server.ts`
- `tsconfig.json` — as in quirk #2.
- `.gitignore`, `.env.example` (PORT, and provider fields for later).
- `scripts/copy-assignments.mjs` — `cp` each dir under `cline-proof/reference/fixtures/` into `assignments/` (idempotent, skip the `check_fixtures.py` helper and any compiled `main` binary).
- `src/config.ts` — `PORT` (default 3000), timeouts (`RUN_TIMEOUT_MS=5000`, `BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS=10000`).
- `src/types.ts` — `Assignment { id, language, statement, build?, run, tests[] }`, `TestCase { name, input, expected }`, `TestResult { name, passed, expected, actual?, error?, timedOut? }`, `RunReport { buildOk, buildError?, results[] }`.
- `src/assignments.ts` — `listAssignments()` (scan `assignments/*/tests.json`), `loadAssignment(id)` (validate id ∈ known set, reject `..`/slashes), zod-validate shape.
- `src/sandbox.ts` — `createSandbox(assignmentId, code)`: `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "hintlab-"))`, copy template, overwrite the code file (`main.py` for python, `main.c` for c).
- `src/runner.ts` — `runAssignment(assignment, sandboxDir)`:
  - if `build` present: run it in `sandboxDir` (timeout, capture stderr); non-zero ⇒ build failure.
  - for each test: run `run` command with test `input` on stdin; `got = stdout.strip()`; `passed = got === expected`; timeout ⇒ `timedOut`.
  - **Key detail**: use `child_process.spawn(cmd, { shell:true, cwd: sandboxDir, env: minimal, timeout })`, write `input` to `child.stdin`, capture `stdout`/`stderr`; on timeout kill the process **group** (`detached:true` + `process.kill(-pid)`) to avoid orphaned children (e.g. a hung `while True`). Trim with `.strip()` exactly as `check_fixtures.py` does; compare exactly.
- `src/app.ts` + `src/server.ts` — `GET /api/assignments` (list + statement + starter source for prefilling), `POST /api/session` stub: validate `{ assignmentId, code }`, create sandbox, run tests, return `{ sessionId, testResults }` (sessionId placeholder; agent wired in Step 02/03).
- `scripts/check-runner.ts` — run the runner against all 3 assignments using the buggy starter code, print the table, and **exit non-zero if the pass/fail set deviates** from §4.

**How to verify**
- `npm install` clean; `npm run copy-assignments` populates `assignments/`.
- `npm run check-runner` prints exactly the §4 results and exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `npm run dev` then `curl -s -X POST localhost:3000/api/session -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list","code":"nums=list(map(int,input().split()));print(sum(nums))"}'` → all 4 tests **pass** (proves the runner isn't just always-failing); re-run with the buggy code → all 4 fail.

**Risks**
- Shell command handling (use `shell:true` for the trusted `tests.json` commands, but always with `cwd` inside the sandbox).
- Timeout/orphan cleanup must actually kill the process group.
- Path traversal via `assignmentId` — validate against the known directory list, never interpolate raw input into a path.
- Language dispatch (python vs c) must pick the right filename (`main.py` vs `main.c`).
- `.strip()` semantics must match `check_fixtures.py` exactly (no `lower()`, no whitespace collapse).

### Step 02 — HintLab agent module (Cline SDK)

**Goal**: Implement `src/agent.ts` using `ClineCore`, with disabled edit tools, an allow-list approval callback, the `give_hint` tool, interactive sessions, and `next-hint` via `send()`. Add a mock-provider test (no API key) mirroring `sdk-check`.

**Files to create/change**
- `src/agent.ts` — the core of the product:
  - Singleton `cline = await ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })` created once at startup.
  - `giveHint = createTool({ name: "give_hint", description: "Show exactly one hint… level 1 nudge, 2 location, 3 concept. Never include corrected code.", inputSchema: z.object({ level: z.number().int().min(1).max(3), tag: z.string(), text: z.string() }), execute })` — `execute` records the hint into the session and returns `{ shown: true }`.
  - **Allow-list** built per assignment from its exact `build`/`run` strings, e.g. for python: `/^python3 main\.py$/`, `/^python3 main\.py < [\w.-]+$/`, `/^(echo|printf) [\w .-]+ \| python3 main\.py$/`; for C: `/^gcc -Wall -O0 main\.c -o main$/`, `/^\.\/main$/`, `/^\.\/main < [\w.-]+$/`. Also allow `cat <sandbox-relative file>`. **Hardening vs the reference**: replace the reference's `.*` with `[\w .-]+` so `;`, `&`, `|`, backticks, `$()`, `>` and `/` are impossible in the variable part, and anchor with `^…$`. (The reference `echo .* | …` regex would match `echo x; rm -rf / | python3 main.py` — do not copy that gap.)
  - `requestToolApproval(req)`: read `req.input.commands`, map each to string, require **all** to match an allow-list entry; return `{ approved: true }` or `{ approved: false, reason: "Command not on the HintLab allow-list" }`. Reject empty command lists.
  - `startSession(session, assignment, testResults)`:
    - `prompt` includes **absolute** `sandboxDir` paths for the code and `tests.json`, the statement, and the already-computed `testResults`, plus: "Diagnose the root cause, then call `give_hint` once with level 1. Use absolute paths for `read_files`. Never write or show corrected code."
    - `config`: `{ sessionId, providerId, modelId, apiKey, baseUrl, systemPrompt, cwd: sandboxDir, workspaceRoot: sandboxDir, enableTools: true, enableSpawnAgent: false, enableAgentTeams: false, extraTools: [giveHint] }`.
    - `toolPolicies`: `read_files`/`search_codebase` autoApprove true; `run_commands` autoApprove **false**; `editor`/`apply_patch` enabled false; `fetch_web_content` enabled false; `give_hint` autoApprove true.
    - `start({ interactive: true, prompt, config, toolPolicies, capabilities: { requestToolApproval } })`.
  - `cline.subscribe(...)` mapping (`agent_event` → `payload.event` with `content_start`/`content_end` for `contentType` "tool"/"text", plus lifecycle/usage/error) into per-session events; in Step 02 this just logs/collects.
  - `nextHint(session)`: track `lastHintLevel` from `give_hint`; call `cline.send({ sessionId, prompt: "The student is still stuck. Give the next hint level (currently level N)." })`.
  - `systemPrompt`: "You are HintLab, a programming tutor. You may read files and run allow-listed commands. You must never write or show corrected code. Deliver help only through the `give_hint` tool."
- `scripts/agent-mock.test.ts` — port `mock-openai.ts` + `02-clinecore-mock.ts` into a test that asserts: (a) `give_hint` executes and records a hint; (b) an allow-listed command is approved; (c) a non-allow-listed command (`rm -rf /tmp/x`, `cat /etc/passwd`) is **blocked** (`approved:false`) and not executed; (d) `editor`/`apply_patch` are absent from the model's tool list; (e) `send()` follow-up works (interactive session).

**How to verify**
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/agent-mock.test.ts` runs with no API key and all assertions pass.
- (Optional, with a real key) a `smoke:real` equivalent of `03-real-provider-smoke.ts` produces one hint for `sum-of-list`.

**Risks**
- Exact built-in tool names/IDs to disable in `@cline/sdk` 0.0.90 — need to enumerate **all** write-capable tools (`editor`, `apply_patch`, and possibly `write_to_file`) and all network tools; missing one = a way for the model to mutate files.
- Allow-list too strict ⇒ agent can't re-run tests; too loose ⇒ sandbox escape. Pre-write per-test input files (`tests/input-<name>.txt`) in the sandbox so the agent can use `< tests/input-basic.txt` instead of inventing pipes.
- `give_hint` must auto-approve so it's never blocked, but its `execute` is the only hint sink.
- The model might bypass `give_hint` and print an answer/code as plain text — system prompt must forbid this, and the UI should surface only `give_hint` payloads as "hints".
- `send()` silently no-ops without `interactive: true` — asserted in the mock test.

---

### Step 03 — SSE streaming + real session endpoints

**Goal**: Wire the agent into HTTP: `POST /api/session` creates the session, runs tests, and **starts the agent in the background**; `GET /api/session/:id/stream` streams agent steps/hints; `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint` calls `send()`.

**Files to create/change**
- `src/sessions.ts` — in-memory `Map<sessionId, Session>` where `Session = { id, assignmentId, code, sandboxDir, testResults, status, hints[], steps[], subscribers:Set<SSE client>, lastHintLevel, agentSessionId }`. Include a TTL/cleanup.
- `src/sse.ts` — `openSse(res)` (headers `text/event-stream`, `cache-control: no-cache`, `connection: keep-alive`), `sendEvent(res, name, data)` → `event: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n`, a heartbeat `: ping` every ~15s, and buffered-event **replay** for late joiners.
- `src/app.ts` (routes):
  - `POST /api/session`: zod-validate body; create sandbox; run tests (Step 01 runner); store session; **fire-and-forget** `agent.startSession(...)` (subscribe first so no events are missed); return `{ sessionId, testResults }` immediately.
  - `GET /api/session/:id/stream`: register the SSE client, replay buffered steps/hints, stream live events (`tool_start`, `tool_result`, `hint`, `text`, `status`, `done`, `error`).
  - `POST /api/session/:id/next-hint`: if the agent is still running return `409`; else call `agent.nextHint()` and let the resulting hint arrive over SSE.
  - Map agent events: `content_start`/`content_end` (contentType `tool` → tool name + input/output/error; contentType `text` → text), lifecycle → `done`/`error`. `give_hint` execute → `hint` event.
- `src/server.ts` — create the `ClineCore` singleton before listening; start listening.

**How to verify**
- `npm run dev`; `POST /api/session` returns `testResults` instantly; `curl -N localhost:3000/api/session/<id>/stream` shows tool calls then a level-1 hint; `POST /api/session/<id>/next-hint` yields a level-2 hint on the same stream.
- Reconnect a second stream after completion → sees replayed history then `done`.
- Kill-path: an invalid provider config produces an `error` event on the stream, not a hung request.

**Risks**
- SSE lifecycle/leaks (client disconnect cleanup), and memory growth (session TTL).

1 | # HintLab
  2 | 
  3 | A debugging tutor for programming labs. A student pastes code and picks an
  4 | assignment; the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases in a
  5 | sandbox, then a Cline‑SDK agent diagnoses the failure and delivers **tiered
  6 | hints** (level 1 nudge → level 2 where to look → level 3 concept). It **never**
  7 | writes or reveals the fix.
  8 | 
  9 | This is **Step 02**: the HintLab tutor agent (built with `@cline/sdk`), wired
 10 | into the Express server. There is no web UI yet.
 11 | 
 12 | ## Requirements
 13 | 
 14 | - Node.js 22+ (verified on Node 24)
 15 | - Python 3 (`python3`) on PATH
 16 | - `gcc` on PATH (for the C assignment)
 17 | - A Cline CLI installation already authenticated with ClinePass (see
 18 |   [Agent credentials](#agent-credentials))
 19 | 
 20 | ## Install
 21 | 
 22 | ```sh
 23 | npm install
 24 | ```
 25 | 
 26 | ## Agent credentials (picked up from `~/.cline`)
 27 | 
 28 | The agent uses the same ClinePass provider/model as the Cline CLI:
 29 | 
 30 | - provider id: `cline-pass`
 31 | - model id: `cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro`
 32 | 
 33 | The SDK does **not** need an API key in the repo or in env vars. In local
 34 | backend mode (`backendMode: "local"`), `ClineCore.start` resolves credentials
 35 | itself from the Cline CLI's config/data directory:
 36 | 
 37 | - `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json` → the `cline-pass` entry, whose
 38 |   `settings.auth` holds the OAuth `accessToken`/`refreshToken`. When
 39 |   `config.apiKey` is omitted, the SDK's local runtime host resolves the
 40 |   provider's OAuth token from this file (refreshing it if expired) and injects
 41 |   it for the request.
 42 | 
 43 | Treat `~/.cline` as read-only: the server never writes to it, and never logs
 44 | any token/secret (it only ever prints provider/model names). You can override
 45 | the provider/model via env vars:
 46 | 
 47 | ```sh
 48 | HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=cline-pass HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro npm start
 49 | ```
 50 | 
 51 | ## Start the server
 52 | 
 53 | ```sh
 54 | npm run dev      # watch mode
 55 | npm start        # run once (tsx src/server.ts)
 56 | ```
 57 | 
 58 | The server listens on `http://localhost:3000` by default. Override with `PORT`:
 59 | 
 60 | ```sh
 61 | PORT=3200 npm start
 62 | ```
 63 | 
 64 | ### Endpoints
 65 | 
 66 | | Method | Path                          | Description                                                      |
 67 | | ------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
 68 | | GET    | `/api/health`                 | Liveness check                                                   |
 69 | | GET    | `/api/assignments`            | List assignments (id, language, statement, starter code)         |
 70 | | POST   | `/api/session`                | Run a submission + start the agent. Body `{ assignmentId, code? }` |
 71 | | GET    | `/api/session/:id/stream`     | Server-Sent Events (replay + live) for the session               |
 72 | | POST   | `/api/session/:id/next-hint`  | Ask the agent for the next hint level (2, then 3)                |
 73 | 
 74 | `POST /api/session` runs the sandboxed runner, creates a session, starts the
 75 | agent in the background asking for a **level‑1** hint, and immediately returns
 76 | `{ sessionId, testResults }`. If `code` is omitted, the assignment's starter
 77 | program is used. Unknown session ids return `404`; `next-hint` returns `409`
 78 | while the agent is still busy, and `{ level: 3, status: "complete" }` once all
 79 | three levels have been delivered.
 80 | 
 81 | ```sh
 82 | curl -s -X POST localhost:3200/api/session \
 83 |   -H 'content-type: application/json' \
 84 |   -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list"}'
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | ### SSE event types
 88 | 
 89 | The stream maps the SDK's `cline.subscribe` events (filtered by `sessionId`) to
 90 | these named events:
 91 | 
 92 | | Event            | Meaning                                                       |
 93 | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
 94 | | `test_results`   | The runner's test results (inputs / expected / got)           |
 95 | | `agent_text`     | Assistant text (`content_start`/`content_end`, type `text`)   |
 96 | | `reasoning`      | Model reasoning summaries (if the provider emits them)        |
 97 | | `tool_call`      | A tool call started (name + input)                            |
 98 | | `tool_result`    | A tool call finished (name + output/error)                    |
 99 | | `approval`       | A `run_commands` approval decision (allowed/denied + commands + reason) |
100 | | `hint`           | An accepted hint delivered through `give_hint`                |
101 | | `hint_rejected`  | A hint rejected by the guard (wrong level or code detected)   |
102 | | `status`         | Session status / iteration / usage / notice updates           |
103 | | `error`          | An agent error (often recoverable)                            |
104 | | `done`           | The agent finished a turn                                     |
105 | 
106 | A `: ping` heartbeat comment is sent every ~15s; buffered events are replayed
107 | to late-joining clients.
108 | 
109 | ## Safety model
110 | 
111 | - The agent runs with `enableSpawnAgent: false` and `enableAgentTeams: false`.
112 | - All file-editing/network tools are disabled (`editor`, `apply_patch`,
113 |   `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` →
114 |   `{ enabled: false }`). `read_files` and `search_codebase` are auto-approved.
115 | - `run_commands` is `autoApprove: false` and gated by a strict regex allow-list
116 |   in `capabilities.requestToolApproval` (see `src/allowlist.ts`). Only the
117 |   assignment's own build/run/read commands are allowed; `;`, `&&`, `||`,
118 |   backticks, `$(`, extra pipes and other redirects are rejected. Every approval
119 |   decision is logged as an `approval` event.
120 | - Hints can only be delivered through `give_hint`, and every hint is checked by
121 |   `src/hintGuard.ts` before it is stored/sent. A hint containing a fenced code
122 |   block, long inline code, code-like lines, or a rewritten solution is rejected
123 |   (the model gets an error and rephrases without code).
124 | 
125 | ## Run the checks
126 | 
127 | ```sh
128 | npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
129 | npm run test:runner   # sandboxed runner against the 3 buggy programs
130 | npm run check:agent   # end-to-end, REAL model call (starts a server on :3200)
131 | ```
132 | 
133 | `test:runner` runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starter programs
134 | and asserts the exact expected pass/fail of every test, plus a correct solution
135 | for each assignment, an infinite-loop program (must time out), and a C program
136 | with a compile error (must report a build failure).
137 | 
138 | `check:agent` unit-tests the allow-list (including injection attempts like
139 | `python3 main.py; rm -rf ~` and `cat /etc/passwd`) and the hint guard, then
140 | starts the server on `PORT=3200`, posts a `sum-of-list` session, reads the SSE
141 | stream, and requests hints level 2 and 3. It asserts exactly one accepted hint
142 | per level, that no hint contains code, that no edit/write tool was executed, and
143 | that any denied command was not run. It prints the hints verbatim, the distinct
144 | SSE event types, and the approval decisions, and exits non-zero on failure
145 | (overall timeout 8 minutes). It leaves no server running.
146 | 
147 | ## Typecheck / build
148 | 
149 | ```sh
150 | npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
151 | npm run build       # tsc
152 | ```

- comparing a cleaned string variable for equality against its reversed slice (e.g., `s.lower() == s.lower()[::-1]` or `t == t[::-1]`)
- a range call that starts at one and ends at the length of the nums list (e.g., `range(1, len(nums))`)
- the sum variable divided by n (e.g., `sum / n` or `total / n`)
- indexing nums with i (e.g., `nums[i]`)
- reversing s with a slice (e.g., `s[::-1]`)
- a C-style float cast of sum divided by n (e.g., `(float) sum / n`)

In general: identifiers combined with code syntax such as:
- call parentheses `foo(` (but the existing CODE_FUNCTION_RE covers builtins; need to also catch arbitrary identifier followed by `(`? No — "programming keywords on their own are not code". But "identifiers combined with code syntax such as call parentheses" — hmm. Actually call parentheses: `range(1, len(nums))` already covered by CODE_FUNCTION_RE (range, len). The description says "identifiers combined with code syntax such as call parentheses, square-bracket indexing or slicing, comparison or arithmetic operators between identifiers, casts, or semicolons."

So the new patterns should detect:
1. Square-bracket indexing/slicing: `ident[...]` e.g. `nums[i]`, `s[::-1]`, `t[::-1]`, `s.lower()[::-1]`.
2. Comparison operators between identifiers: `a == b`, `s == s[::-1]`.
3. Arithmetic operators between identifiers: `sum / n`, `total + nums[i]`, `sum / n` (division).
4. Casts: `(float)`, `(int)`, etc. — already covered by CODE_LINE_PATTERNS `(?:\\(float\\)|\\(int\\)|...)`.

### SSE event types

The stream only ever forwards a small **allow-list** of event types, each with a
sanitised payload that can never contain the model's own text, reasoning, or raw
SDK/stack-trace messages. Unguarded events (`agent_text`, `reasoning`, and tool
inputs/outputs that carry model free text) are dropped at the server boundary and
are never sent — including to late joiners via the replay buffer.

| Event            | What reaches the client                                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_results`   | Test results (name, input, expected, got, pass/fail, signal/timedOut, build error) — never `sandboxDir` |
| `tool_call`      | Only `run_commands` (command), `read_files` (file name), or `run_tests` (test name) |
| `tool_result`    | For `run_commands` a short trimmed output; for `run_tests` the pass/fail summary |
| `approval`       | `allowed`/`denied` + the command (or tool name)               |
| `hint`           | An accepted, guarded hint (`level`, `tag`, `text`)            |
| `hint_status` / `hint_rejected` | Only a reason category (e.g. `wrong level`, `contained code`) — never the rejected text |
| `status`         | Session status string only (`running`/`idle`/`complete`/`error`) |
| `error`          | A short, friendly human line (no stack traces / raw SDK messages) |
| `done`           | The agent finished a turn (reason only)                       |

A `: ping` heartbeat comment is sent every ~15s; buffered events are replayed to
late-joining clients through the same filter.

## Safety model

- The agent runs with `enableSpawnAgent: false` and `enableAgentTeams: false`.
- All file-editing/network tools are disabled (`editor`, `apply_patch`,
  `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` →
  `{ enabled: false }`). `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, and
  `run_tests` are auto-approved.
- The built-in `run_commands` tool is **disabled** (`enabled: false`). Instead the
  agent gets a custom `run_tests` tool that runs the student's code through the
  hardened server runner (process-group kill, per-test timeouts, minimal env with
  `HOME` set to the sandbox dir, signal reporting) — so student code run by the
  agent can never read server env vars or the credentials in `~/.cline`.
- `requestToolApproval` still denies everything that is not explicitly allowed, so
  any command attempt is blocked and shown as an approval-denied line. The strict
  regex allow-list in `src/allowlist.ts` is retained and unit-tested; it allows
  only `python3 main.py`, the exact `gcc` build command, `./main`, a stdin
  redirect from an `input-*.txt` file, and `cat` of `main.py`/`main.c`/`tests.json`
  or an `input-*.txt` file. Any `$` (variable/command expansion) and any pipe
  (`echo … | program`) are denied. Each test's input is written to its own
  `input-<test-name>.txt` file in the workdir.
- Hints can only be delivered through `give_hint`, and every hint is checked by
  `src/hintGuard.ts` before it is stored/sent. A hint containing a fenced code
  block, inline code, a one-line code expression (indexing/slicing, comparison or
  arithmetic between identifiers, casts, calls, semicolons), or a rewritten
  solution is rejected — while plain prose like "for x in the list" or "if the
  list is empty" still passes.

## Run the checks

```sh
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
npm run test:runner   # sandboxed runner against the 3 buggy programs
npm run check:agent   # end-to-end, REAL model call (starts a server on :3200)

```

`test:runner` runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starter programs
and asserts the exact expected pass/fail of every test, plus a correct solution
for each assignment, an infinite-loop program (must time out), and a C program
with a compile error (must report a build failure).

`check:agent` unit-tests the allow-list (including `$`-expansion and pipe
injection attempts like `echo $HOME | python3 main.py`) and the hint guard (new
one-line code expressions are rejected; prose like "for x in the list" passes),
then starts the server on `PORT=3200`, posts a `sum-of-list` session, reads the
SSE stream, and requests hints level 2 and 3. It asserts exactly one accepted hint
per level, that no hint contains code, that **no `agent_text`/`reasoning` and no
rejected hint text arrive over SSE**, that `run_commands` was never executed (and
never approved), that `run_tests` was used (or tests were otherwise reported), and
that no edit/write tool ran. It prints the hints verbatim, the distinct SSE event
types, and the approval decisions, and exits non-zero on failure (overall timeout
8 minutes). It leaves no server running.

`check:web` starts the server on `PORT=3200`, fetches `/` (asserting the page
loads with the app title and that `/app.js` and `/style.css` return 200), fetches
`/api/assignments`, starts one real session on `is-palindrome` (or
`average-marks`), reads the SSE stream until the level-1 hint (or a timeout), and
asserts the event types contain no `agent_text`/`reasoning`. It prints the event
types seen and the hint, then stops the server by PID. It leaves no server running.

- `src/runner.ts` — added `slugifyTestName` + `runTestsInWorkdir` (hardened runner for the agent); writes `input-<test-name>.txt` per test into the workdir.
- `src/hintGuard.ts` — blocks one-line code expressions (indexing/slicing `nums[i]`, `s[::-1]`; comparison `t == t[::-1]`; arithmetic `sum / n`; casts `(float) sum / n`; semicolons) while letting prose like "for x in the list" / "if the list is empty" through; added `categorizeHintReason`.
- `src/app.ts` — sanitises the `POST /api/session` response (no `sandboxDir`).
- `scripts/check-agent.ts` — new allow-list unit tests ($/pipe denials), new hint-guard blocked/prose cases, and the new SSE contract assertions (no `agent_text`/`reasoning`, no rejected hint text, `run_commands` never executed/approved, `run_tests` used).
- `package.json` — added `check:web`.
- `README.md` — UI usage, new SSE event contract, `check:web`, updated safety model.

## SSE event types that now reach the client

Explicit allow-list: `test_results`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `approval`, `hint`, `hint_status`, `hint_rejected`, `status`, `error`, `done`. `agent_text` and `reasoning` are never sent. During the live `check:agent` run the stream produced exactly: `done, hint, status, test_results, tool_call, tool_result`.

## New allow-list (`src/allowlist.ts`)

- Allowed: `python3 main.py`, `python3 main.py < input-*.txt`, `gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main`, `./main`, `./main < input-*.txt`, and `cat` of `main.py` / `main.c` / `tests.json` / `input-*.txt`.
- Denied: any `$` (variable/command expansion), any `|` (pipes), plus the existing `;`, `&&`, `||`, backtick, `>`, `&`, newline/CR, `*`, `?`.
